translation_notes: the flagged site is `rdflib.Literal(trans, dest_lang)`: the SECOND POSITIONAL argument of Literal is `lang`, so this is a language literal whose tag is computed (a module global set per task: "en" or "de"). Translated as `{trans}@{dest_lang}` (the computed-tag form `{v}@{k}`, ldpy 0.7.1), in a `+{ {triple["s"]} {prop} {trans}@{dest_lang} }(graph)`; `prop` is a module global holding a URIRef, interpolated as the predicate.

`trans` is NOT always a str: on the cache hit it is `trans_cached[s].strip()`, but otherwise it is the googletrans Translated OBJECT (the source never takes `.text`), so the literal's lexical form is str(Translated) -- 'Translated(src=ru, dest=en, text=..., ...)'. `{trans}@{dest_lang}` reproduces this as is (`Literal(trans, lang=...)`, no coercion in between), which the driver pins by comparing both cases; the tag only has to be a str (`langtag` raises on None, where Literal(trans, None) would give a plain literal -- unreachable here, dest_lang is NameError until configure_task sets it).

the assembled query string `"SELECT ?s ?o WHERE {?s <" + str(prop) + "> ?o .}"` + `ingraph.query(query)` becomes `m{ ?s {prop} ?o }(ingraph)` (a basic graph pattern, the predicate interpolated in term position, `(ingraph)` as receiver); the loop body is untouched and still reads `triple["s"]` / `triple["o"]` (ldpy's Row accepts the variable names). INSTRUCTIONS section 2 forbids the assembled query, hence this change outside the flagged site.

prefixes: none declared (no vocabulary term is written in the region). The vocabulary (jlo, skos) comes from the project's own module and stays Python Namespaces (`prop = skos.prefLabel` is set by configure_task, outside the region).

context shim (context_shim.py): `from ._dataset_command import ...` imports django/scrapy/toml, `googletrans` is a Google Translate web client (not installed, network). The shim has jlo/skos with the real IRIs, the two loggers (same name as the source's), an empty DatasetCommand, a table-driven Translator whose Translated has the shape of googletrans's __str__ (a text the service does not know comes back unchanged, still Cyrillic; "Раввин" is answered as a banned client, src != ru), and configure_task copied from the source (it takes the module's globals). original.py / translated.ldpy get `translator = Translator()` (a module line of the source outside the region) and the same `run(task, ingraph)` harness at the end: it sets `prop` / `dest_lang` through configure_task and returns the written graph, since the region reads three module globals (prop, dest_lang, translator) it does not define.

driver: five calls through run(): en-label (4 labels, one unknown to the service -> error log, one banned -> src != ru branch, renewal of translator), de-label on the same graph (cache hits tagged @de; the cache is per subject, not per language: the source's behaviour), en-abstract (the other predicate; two subjects cached by the labels, two that only have an abstract), de-abstract, and an empty graph. The log records (INFO from log/error) are compared as a multiset: the cached / translated / Cyrillic / banned branches show up there. fixture.ttl has skos:altLabel and skos:definition neighbours that must not be read.

anti-hollow-green: tag fixed to @en, no tag, `.text` instead of the object, tag from src_lang, pattern widened to ?p, predicate fixed to skos:prefLabel: rdfeval check FAILED each time; restored, green.
optimization_notes: Python: the assembled SELECT string and `ingraph.query(query)` become `ingraph.subject_objects(prop)`, unpacked in the `for` (the `query`, `res` and `triple` names go); `trans.text.strip()`, computed three times, is read once into `text`; the two `if trans.src=="ru"` tests merge into one, the Cyrillic check nested inside it (same log order).

LD Python: the same restructuring; only the source of the loop (`m{ ?s {prop} ?o }(ingraph)`, tuples unpacked) and the write (`+{ {subject} {prop} {trans}@{dest_lang} }(graph)`) differ from optimized.py. No exception to the symmetry rule.

The rereading already removes the assembled query that the faithful translation replaced with m{ }: once optimized.py reads the graph with `subject_objects`, the m{ } gains nothing on top (notation ratio about 1.0).
header_optimization_notes: Both sides: DatasetCommand, jlo and skos go from the shim import (the shim's configure_task reads its own jlo/skos); log, error, Translator, configure_task, rdflib and re stay. The header has no @prefix, and stays identical on both sides.
